title: Merging of Bayes and quasi-Bayes empirical Bayes procedures for Poisson compound decisions
summary: The Poisson compound decision problem is a long-standing problem in statistics, in which empirical Bayes methods are used to estimate Poisson means under a mixture model. We study this problem from the viewpoint of $g$-modeling, comparing two nonparametric strategies for estimating the unknown mixing distribution: a Bayesian empirical Bayes strategy, based on the Dirichlet process posterior, and a quasi-Bayesian empirical Bayes strategy, based on Newton's algorithm. The latter is computationally attractive, but its relationship with the Bayesian strategy requires theoretical justification.…
